parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Gradient of tangent $=-\dfrac12$ — B1 OE, SOI
Gradient of normal $=2$ — M1; use $m_1m_2=-1$ with their numerical tangent gradient.
$\dfrac{y-3}{x-4}=2$, so $y=2x-5$ — A1 OE, ISW; allow $y=2x+c$, $3=2\times4+c\Rightarrow c=-5$.
Total: 3

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
First two marks, Method 1: $-1-3=2(-\dfrac12p-4)$ or $-1=-p-5$ — M1*; use their stated centre $(\dfrac{\pm p}{2},\pm1)$ in their normal equation.
$p=-4$ — A1
Method 2: $-1=2x-5\Rightarrow x=2\Rightarrow-\dfrac12p=2$ — M1*; use their normal and stated centre; $p=-4$ — A1.
Method 3: $2x+2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}+p+2\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$ — M1*; with $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac12$, $p=-4$ — A1.
Last three marks, Method 1: $r^2=(4-2)^2+(3-(-1))^2=20$ — M1*; use $(4,3)$ and their centre to find $r^2$ or $r$.
$-q+1+\dfrac14p^2=20$ — DM1 OE; equate their expression for $r^2$ to their $20$.
$q=-15$ — A1
Method 2: $r=\dfrac{|2-2-10|}{\sqrt5}=\dfrac{10}{\sqrt5}$ — M1*; use $(2,-1)$ and $x+2y-10=0$.
$-q+1+\dfrac14p^2=(\dfrac{10}{\sqrt5})^2$ — DM1 OE; $q=-15$ — A1.
Method 3: $4^2+3^2+4p+6+q=0\Rightarrow4p+q+31=0$ — M1*; substitute $(4,3)$ into their circle, or use their completed-square equation.
$4(-4)+q+31=0$ — DM1; substitute their $p=-4$.
$q=-15$ — A1
Alternative simultaneous tangent method: substitute the tangent or normal into the circle and use $x=4$ or $y=3$ to form $4p+q+31=0$ — M1*.
Solve tangent and circle simultaneously to form a quadratic, then use $b^2-4ac=0$ to obtain $p^2-12p-139-5q=0$ — M1*.
Solve simultaneously to find $p$ or $q$ — DM1; $p=-4$ — A1; $q=-15$ — A1.
Total: 5
